title: 100K+ plays later: I made a game with Claude where you try to time the market and beat a couch. The couch wins 62% of the time.
author: noir_chat
selftext:
**The game.** [beatthecouch.com](http://beatthecouch.com/) \- $10,000, two secret years of real S&P 500 history, one buy / sell button. Your opponent is a couch. It buys on day one and never sells. After each game, 1,000 monkeys replay your trade count on random days. Beat 90% of them or your win is stamped Lucky.

**The data.** 100,278 games (at the time of the graph - now around 107K, still similar). The couch won 62%. Humans only seem to beat the couch when the market crashed in their window.

**What Claude did.** The data pipeline (S&P closes 1928 to 2025, dividends, T-bills etc). The whole game as one HTML file and the Cloudflare backend. And also the reddit app port at [reddit.com/r/beatthecouch](http://reddit.com/r/beatthecouch)

comments.author: pavelkomin
comments.body: Very nice idea but very hard to play when you have 0.5 seconds for a decision. You need to add an option to go at least 0.01 of the original speed, or just make the player make a decision each day.

replies.author: noir_chat
replies.body: I might look into a 0.1x mode, thanks for the feedback

comments.author: aphant-
comments.body: I played around 10 times and got massive bull runs on the majority. Sample is anecdotal but it got me thinking on how the 2-year periods were picked. Assuming that they were picked intentionally, focusing on years with large swings, how many of those favour couch?

replies.author: noir_chat
replies.body: It includes all permutations of 2 years so i think you just got (un)lucky

comments.author: Prophysaon_Coeruleum
comments.body: You need to clean up the website homepage. It's information overload. The only important button you have is "play now" - save the rest of the info for later.

comments.author: Worried_Number5115
comments.body:
I like the game & it’s a nice concept imo but visually it’s lacking in terms of UI. 

I’d like the ability to set the speed of how fast it goes through the chart & how many years are in the timeframe.

comments.author: UpDown
comments.body: 10% of players beating 90% of random monkeys is actually also luck.
